title: Pizza al Tartufo
subtitle: Pizza with black truffle, mozzarella, and fontina
excerpt: Pizza al tartufo is a white pizza: no tomato sauce: with fontina, mozzarella, and black truffle. It is a northern and central Italian pizza that showcases the truffle rather than pairing it with acidic tomato. The cheese base is gentle enough to let the earthy, pungent truffle come through. Truffle oil is a reasonable off-season substitute, though it is a different thing.
sourceNotes: Pizza al tartufo is associated with the truffle-producing regions of central Italy, particularly Umbria (Norcia, Spoleto) and Le Marche. Fresh black truffle from the Apennine mountains is in season November to March. White pizza (pizza bianca) as a base for truffle is a modern restaurant style.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Dough can be cold-proved 24 to 3 days ahead.
recipe.temperatureNote: maximum oven temperature, pizza stone or steel

content.text: Pizza al tartufo is a white pizza: the base is cheese and olive oil with no tomato, which would compete with the truffle. Fontina melts smoothly and has a mild, slightly funky quality that works with truffle; mozzarella adds stretch. The truffle goes on raw after the pizza comes out of the oven, shaved directly over the hot cheese where the warmth releases its aroma. Fresh black truffle is the correct ingredient; truffle oil gives a related but different result.

items.prepNote: fior di latte, drained and sliced

content.text: Make the dough (flour, water, yeast, salt, olive oil), knead 8 to 10 minutes, divide into 4 balls, and cold-prove 24 to 48 hours. Preheat pizza stone at 250°C fan for 45 to 60 minutes.

Roll or stretch each dough ball to a 28 to 30 cm round. Transfer to baking paper. Drizzle the base with olive oil. Arrange the fontina and mozzarella slices over the base, leaving a 1.5 cm rim. Season lightly with pepper.
Slide the pizza onto the hot stone. Bake for 7 to 10 minutes until the base is crisp and the cheese is melted and slightly golden at the edges.

Remove from the oven and immediately shave fresh black truffle generously over the hot pizza using a mandoline or truffle slicer. Serve at once: the truffle fragrance is most intense in the first 2 minutes.

items.cause: Truffle was added too late, after the pizza cooled, so it couldn't release its volatile compounds in the heat
items.fix: Add the truffle immediately on removing from the oven, while the cheese is still bubbling. The warmth releases the aromatic compounds.

items.symptom: Fontina is stringy and doesn't melt smoothly
items.fix: Slice fontina thinly: no more than 3 mm. Thick slices take longer to melt and can become stringy rather than flowing.

items.symptom: Base is pale and soft despite hot oven
items.fix: The stone must preheat for a full 45 to 60 minutes. For a white pizza with no tomato, the base colour comes entirely from the stone's direct heat.

content.text: Black truffle pizza is linked to the truffle-growing areas of central Italy: Norcia in Umbria and the hills of Le Marche. The fresh black truffle season runs from November to March. During this time it appears on pizza in every restaurant in the area.
